claims.text: An ML-guided inverse-design approach can identify alloy compositions and processing routes that concurrently improve strength and ductility.
Integrating processing–microstructure–property relationships enables the inverse-design approach to generate tailored microstructures.
Tailored microstructures can break the traditional strength–ductility trade-off.
The initial homogeneous alloy system typically exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off under conventional processing.
An ML-guided inverse-design framework can select optimal alloy compositions and processing conditions.
The selected compositions and processing conditions promote beneficial microstructural features.
Controlled grain size can favor both high strength and enhanced ductility.
A controlled precipitate distribution can favor both high strength and enhanced ductility.
Dual-phase mixtures can favor both high strength and enhanced ductility.
The ML model can identify nonlinear correlations in extensive experimental and simulation datasets.
The correlations identified by the model can reveal processing routes and alloy chemistries that refine grains.
The correlations identified by the model can reveal processing routes and alloy chemistries that produce evenly distributed strengthening phases.
Refined grains and evenly distributed strengthening phases can simultaneously improve yield strength and ductility.
The ML-designed alloy and processing route will produce concurrent increases in strength and ductility relative to conventional processing.
Conventional alloying and heat-treatment methods often improve strength at the expense of ductility, or vice versa.
The predictions are expected to apply only within the alloy-chemistry and processing-parameter ranges represented in the training data.
Extrapolation beyond the training-data range may produce unforeseen behavior.
The reliability of the approach depends on the quality and completeness of its datasets.
